name: Royal Trux
label: Drag City
lede: A Pussy Galore guitarist and his teenage girlfriend sawed rock and roll into pieces on a San Francisco double LP, launched Drag City, cashed a Virgin check worth over a million dollars, and ended it all in a Guardian interview.

eras.title: Out of Pussy Galore
eras.text: Neil Hagerty was a teenage guitarist in Jon Spencer's Pussy Galore, the D.C. noise band that treated rock history like scrap metal. On the side he and Jennifer Herrema, still in her teens, started a band of their own that would outlast his day job.

years.h: Neil Hagerty talks [[Pussy Galore|cf97d78e-7c86-4931-92c0-b8e22bae1e33]] into remaking Exile on Main St.
years.p: Per Wikipedia, teenage guitarist Neil Hagerty convinced his Pussy Galore bandmates to record their own full cassette-only version of the Rolling Stones' Exile on Main St.

years.h: Neil Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema start Royal Trux in D.C.
years.p: Neil Hagerty, in his early twenties, and Jennifer Herrema, in her late teens, start Royal Trux in Washington, D.C. Hagerty sees Pussy Galore as a job; Royal Trux is the real thing.

years.h: Royal Trux: the debut, on the band's own label
years.p: The first Royal Trux album comes out on their own Royal label: Neil Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema's songs sawn into pieces and stuck back together.

eras.title: The band that started Drag City
eras.text: Two Chicago record fans, Dan Koretzky and Dan Osborn, started Drag City because of Royal Trux. The duo repaid them with the label's first single, its first album, and a talent scout's eye that brought in Will Oldham.

years.h: Hero/Zero: Drag City's first release
years.p: Dan Koretzky and Dan Osborn start Drag City after hearing Royal Trux, and the band's Hero/Zero 7-inch is the label's first record.

years.h: Twin Infinitives, a double LP built in a San Francisco flat
years.p: Recorded October 1989 to June 1990 at Lowdown in San Francisco, Twin Infinitives is Drag City's first full-length: fifteen songs over four sides, including the 14-minute (Edge of the) Ape Oven.
years.xp:
The couple were living near the poverty line in San Francisco. According to Stereogum, they tracked the album sober but judged the mixes under various substances, a marijuana test and an LSD test among them.

NME and Uncut gave it 9/10. Drowned in Sound gave it 5.

years.h: Untitled, a.k.a. the Skulls record
years.p: The third Royal Trux album is their first built from conventional songs, made on an 8-track. Stereogum calls it the band's first clean record.

years.h: Royal Trux take [[Smog|89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34]]'s Bill Callahan on his first tour
years.p: Royal Trux bring Drag City labelmate [[Bill Callahan|c309d914-93af-4b3f-8058-d79c75ea89da]], then recording as Smog, on his first tour. Neil Hagerty later produces Callahan records.

years.h: Royal Trux push Drag City to sign [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]]
years.p: Neil Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema talk Drag City into signing [[Palace|44d766e3-fc4a-4c19-9cdc-cd69966de1d8]]'s Will Oldham, and produce the Palace Brothers single Come In as Adam and Eve.

years.h: Cats and Dogs, and a fan named Kurt Cobain
years.p: Royal Trux add guitarist Michael Kaiser and drummer Ian Willers for Cats and Dogs. Stereogum notes [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] was apparently a fan.

years.h: Lollapalooza side stage: heckled as "Axl Rose!"
years.p: Royal Trux play the 1993 Lollapalooza side stage, where Jennifer Herrema gets heckled with shouts of "Axl Rose!"

eras.title: A million dollars of Virgin money
eras.text: After Nirvana, majors went shopping for credibility, and Virgin bought Royal Trux. The money paid for a house and studio in rural Virginia, a real rhythm section, and a clean break from heroin. It did not buy Virgin the record it wanted.

years.h: Virgin signs Royal Trux for over $1 million
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Virgin gave Royal Trux a three-album deal worth more than $1 million, looking for indie credibility after Nirvana broke.
years.xp: The duo bought a house in Virginia and turned it into a studio, where they also recorded other bands, [[The Make-Up|26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a]] among them.

years.h: Thank You, produced by Neil Young's man David Briggs
years.p: Royal Trux cut Thank You live in the studio with [[David Briggs|49b65db4-fe20-4a97-9073-55d33e65ac98]], Neil Young's longtime producer, plus bassist Dan Brown and drummer Chris Pyle, son of [[Lynyrd Skynyrd|c544ed4d-2390-4442-a83e-1ea2883b09c8]]'s Artimus Pyle.

years.h: Sweet Sixteen: the cover Virgin couldn't live with
years.p: Recorded at the Virginia ranch studio, Sweet Sixteen left Virgin unhappy. Stereogum says the cover art was the sticking point.

years.h: Royal Trux refuse Virgin a third album and take a severance check
years.p: Royal Trux refuse to make the third Virgin record. Stereogum says the label cut them loose with a fat severance check, which paid for the next album.

years.h: Neil Hagerty publishes a sci-fi novel, Victory Chimp
years.p: Neil Hagerty's science-fiction novel Victory Chimp comes out.

eras.title: Home to Drag City, then apart
eras.text: Back on Drag City with Virgin's money in the bank, Royal Trux made three records in three years, their most straight-up rock. Then the couple's relationship ended on the road, and the band ended with it.

years.h: Accelerator, and a Primal Scream tribute
years.p: Royal Trux return to Drag City with Accelerator, adding keyboardist Tim McClain. [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]]'s Bobby Gillespie liked it enough to name a song Accelerator on 2000's XTRMNTR.

years.h: Veterans of Disorder, with Jon Theodore and David Pajo
years.p: Future [[The Mars Volta|20883363-1ea4-4d72-ad72-c0e767038f3e]] drummer [[Jon Theodore|eeb1d415-4dbc-4038-8b09-4faf8c3c24ba]] and [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]]'s [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] on bass back Royal Trux on Veterans of Disorder.

q: You have to really like music to like our band
years.h: Neil Hagerty on who Royal Trux were for
years.p: Late in the run, Neil Hagerty summed up the band's audience in one line.

years.h: Pound for Pound, the last album of the first run
years.p: The band called Pound for Pound an extension of Blue Is the Frequency, the closer on Veterans of Disorder.

years.h: Neil Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema split, and so does Royal Trux
years.p: The couple's relationship came apart on the 2000 Pound for Pound tour; Stereogum ties it to Jennifer Herrema's relapses after her father's death. Royal Trux end in 2001.

years.h: After Royal Trux: The Howling Hex, RTX, Black Bananas
years.p: Both stay on Drag City. Neil Hagerty records solo and as [[The Howling Hex|beb385d7-b5d9-41a9-a75a-6ac94dcf1c44]]; Jennifer Herrema forms [[RTX|e7720ff7-d4f9-4cfb-ba39-c00e63572d13]], later [[Black Bananas|7fa9cc77-c2fa-4b4c-985a-6707d1794af8]].

eras.title: Reunion, then "I'm out, man"
eras.text: Fourteen years on, the two went back on stage together, made a first album in nineteen years, and fell apart again in public before it could tour.

years.h: Royal Trux reunite at Berserktown in Santa Ana
years.p: Neil Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema play together again at the Berserktown festival in Santa Ana, California.

years.h: Royal Trux at Webster Hall, New York
years.p: The reunion reaches New York's Webster Hall.

years.h: Platinum Tips + Ice Cream, a reunion live album
years.p: Royal Trux release a live album from the reunion shows; in May they play their first UK date since reuniting, at Manchester's Victoria Warehouse.

years.h: Royal Trux sign with Fat Possum
years.p: The Fat Possum deal puts the whole Royal Trux catalog on streaming services.

years.h: White Stuff, the first studio album in 19 years
years.p: Royal Trux release White Stuff on Fat Possum.

q: She steamrollered right over me, man
years.h: Neil Hagerty quits and the White Stuff tour is cancelled
years.p: Neil Hagerty tells the Guardian he isn't touring and didn't approve White Stuff. On April 30 the tour is called off, and both say the reunion is over.
years.xp: Hagerty said Herrema had steamrollered him and that he had no idea what the album was. Herrema answered that he regularly threatened to quit mid-tour. Both have said the reunion ended with White Stuff.
